content:
rachel: Heads-up: found a reproducible cursor drift in the sampleapp when prefetch is enabled + aggressive retry. Users see duplicated or skipped items while paging.

rachel: Repro steps: prefetchWindow=3, network flaps cause page=3 to retry and return slower than page=4; prefetch commits pages to local cache as they finish (no ordering), so UI shows page4 then page3 -> duplicates or gaps.

leo: Yikes. Do we have logs/traces?

rachel: Logs show timestamps and item IDs: 
```
fetch page=3 -> start (correlation=aa1)
fetch page=4 -> start (bb2)
fetch page=4 -> success items ids 301..320
commit page=4 to cache
fetch page=3 -> retry success items ids 281..300
commit page=3 to cache (appending)
```

leo: That commit order will definitely reorder the cursor. Prefetch must maintain logical ordering or buffer until contiguous pages are present.

sam: Parity note: Go SDK had an ordered-commit flag we added for some enterprise customers. JS prefetch defaulted to fast-commit. Looks like a parity gap.

jing: Two immediate fixes: (A) keep a small reorder buffer keyed by page index and only surface pages once contiguous (config: prefetch.reorderWindow=2), or (B) tag commits with sequence and apply an idempotent merge that deduplicates and reorders. Both have tradeoffs for latency.

rachel: For onboarding/demo we should avoid surprises. I'd prefer default conservative behavior: ordered commit with reorderWindow=1 (i.e., wait for previous if missing up to N ms) and a short timeout fallback so we don't block forever.

sam: Implementation details: 1) add per-cursor sequence numbers; 2) prefetch scheduler records page index and places result in a min-heap; 3) commit worker pops while nextIndex available or timeout exceeded; 4) metric `prefetch.commit_out_of_order_count` and `prefetch.reorder_wait_ms`.

leo: Also add integration tests: simulated out-of-order responses and flaky network, assert final combined list equals server-ordered list and no duplicates. Add e2e sampleapp scenario for onboarding.

jing: For parity: add same config to Go/Python SDKs and keep names identical. Add a migration note in changelog and quickstart: "If you see duplicated pages with prefetch enabled, update SDK or set `prefetch.commitPolicy=ordered`."

rachel: I'll open a JS PR with the buffer + timeout approach and unit tests. I'll include a demo harness that intentionally delays page3 to validate behavior.

devex-bot: deploy-bot: created canary build branch "prefetch-ordered-2026" (id d-8209).

sam: Nice. Also consider exposing `prefetch.commitPolicy=last-wins|ordered|merge` so advanced users can choose. Default to ordered for sampleapp.

rachel: Agree. I'll add CLI flag to sampleapp to switch policy for demos. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
